'''Viktor K. Jirsa''' (born 27 June 1968) is a Czech-German [[physicist]] and [[computational neuroscientist]] whose work links large-scale [[Brain simulation|brain modelling]] with [[Neuroimaging|brain imaging]]. He is Director of Research (DRCE) at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) and heads the Institut de Neuroscience des Systèmes (INS UMR1106) at [[Inserm]] [[Aix-Marseille University]]. Since 2022 he serves as Chief Science Officer of the European digital neuroscience infrastructure [[Human Brain Project#Legacy|EBRAINS]].

Since the late 1990s, Jirsa's research focuses on how the [[human brain]]'s function relates to [[network dynamics]]. He pioneered the integration of biologically realistic [[Brain connectivity estimators|connectivity]] into human and rodent brain network models.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Jirsa V |author2=Jantzen K |author3=Fuchs A |author4=Kelso S |title=Spatiotemporal forward solution of the EEG and MEG using network modeling |journal=IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging |date=May 2002 |volume=21 |issue=5 |pages=493–504 |doi=10.1109/TMI.2002.1009385 |s2cid=240149 |pmid=12071620 |bibcode=2002ITMI...21..493J |issn=0278-0062}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Ghosh A |author2=Rho Y |author3=McIntosh R |author4=Kötter R |author5=Jirsa V |title=Noise during Rest Enables the Exploration of the Brain's Dynamic Repertoire |journal=PLOS Computational Biology |date=October 2008 |volume=4 |issue=10 |article-number=e1000196 |doi=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1000196 |doi-access=free |s2cid=15691446 |pmid=18846206 |issn=1553-734X |pmc=2551736 |bibcode=2008PLSCB...4E0196G }}</ref> Clinical applications of his large-scale brain modelling approach are widespread in diagnosis, understanding and therapy of [[epilepsy]]<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Jirsa V |author2=Wang H |author3=Triebkorn P |author4=Hashemi M |author5=Jha J |author6=Gonzalez-Martinez J |author7=Guye M |author8=Makhalova J |author9=Bartolomei F |title=Personalised virtual brain models in epilepsy |journal=The Lancet Neurology |date=May 2023 |volume=22 |issue=5 |pages=443–454 |doi=10.1016/S1474-4422(23)00008-X |s2cid=257718959 |pmid=36972720 |url=https://www.thelancet.com/journals/laneur/article/PIIS1474-4422(23)00008-X/abstract |issn=1474-4465|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[psychiatry]].<ref>{{cite web |title=How & why we build a virtual brain twin |url=https://www.virtualbraintwin.eu/project/how_and_why.html |website=Virtual Brain Twin |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref> Throughout his [[#Academic career|academic career]] Jirsa has played leading roles in [[personalized medicine]] and translational computational neuroscience within the [[Human Brain Project]] (HBP) and other large European initiatives. He is lead scientist of the open source [[neuroinformatics]] platform The Virtual Brain.<ref>{{cite web |title=Leaders |url=https://www.thevirtualbrain.org/tvb/zwei/teamwork-leaders |website=The Virtual Brain |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref> 

==Early life and education==

Jirsa was born in [[Prague]], Czechia and grew up in [[Stuttgart]], Germany. He studied elementary particle physics at the [[University of Manchester]], United Kingdom where he obtained his Master of Science (M.Sc.) in 1991. He then combined philosophy with theoretical physics at the [[University of Stuttgart]], Germany, earning a ''Diplom'' (Master's degree) in 1993, followed by a doctorate (Dr. rer. nat.) in applied mathematics/theoretical physics in 1996, under [[Hermann Haken]]. His postdoctoral work with [[J. A. Scott Kelso]] at the [[Florida Atlantic University]] (FAU) focused on brain and [[Cognitive model#Behavioral_dynamics|behavioral dynamics]] (1997-1998).

==Academic career==

In 1999 Jirsa started as assistant professor at the Florida Atlantic University and founded the Theoretical Neuroscience Group (TNG).<ref>{{cite web |title=Theoretical Neurosciences Group |url=https://ins-amu.fr/tng |website=Institut de Neuroscience des Systèmes |date=22 July 2020 |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref> From 2004 to 2005 he held the role of tenured Associate Professor of Physics of Complex Systems & Brain Sciences. In 2006 Jirsa was recruited as Director of Research for the French Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS) in [[Marseille]], France.<ref name="INS profile">{{cite web |title=Viktor Jirsa |url=https://ins-amu.fr/jirsaviktor |website=Institut de Neuroscience des Systèmes |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref> In 2012 he co-founded the Institut de Neuroscience des Systèmes (INS, Aix-Marseille University) with neurologist Patrick Chauvel, becoming its director in 2014.<ref name="INS profile"/>

Jirsa was a work package leader and member of the Science and Infrastructure Board of the [[Human Brain Project]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Science and Infrastructure Board |url=https://www.humanbrainproject.eu/en/about-hbp/project-structure/governance/science-and-infrastructure-board/ |website=Human Brain Project |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref> before joining the management board of the non-profit successor organization EBRAINS as Chief Science Officer in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=EBRAINS appoints new Chief Science Officer |url=https://www.ebrains.eu/news-and-events/ebrains-appoints-new-chief-science-officer |website=EBRAINS |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref> In this role he guides the European efforts in digital neuroscience to translate multiscale brain models into clinical and industrial applications.

|author1=Woodman M |author2=Pezard L |author3=Domide L |author4=Knock S |author5=Sanz-Leon P |author6=Mersmann J |author7=McIntosh A |author8=Jirsa V |title=Integrating neuroinformatics tools in Jirsa led the work package building The Virtual Brain within the "Brain Network Recovery Group", a consortium of 16 international scientists from computational, cognitive and clinical [[neuroscience]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Who we are |url=https://brain-nrg.squarespace.com/who |website=Brain NRG |access-date=11 October 2025}}</ref> coordinated by Randy McIntosh from 2005 to 2025}}</ref>

In 2018, TVB was integrated as neuroinformatics platform into the [[Human Brain Project]] (HBP),<ref>{{cite web |title=The Virtual Brain neuroinformatics platform joins the HBP |url=https://www.humanbrainproject.eu/en/follow-hbp/news/the-virtual-brain-neuroinformatics-platform-joins-the-eu-s-flagship-human-brain-project/ |website=Human Brain Project |access-date=11 October 2025}}</ref> a €607 million EU scientific research project. Since 2023 TVB is the principal full-brain simulator of the successor organization of HBP, the [[Human Brain Project#Legacy|European Brain Research Infrastructures]] (EBRAINS).<ref>{{cite web |title=The Virtual Brain |url=https://www.ebrains.eu/tools/the-virtual-brain |website=EBRAINS |access-date=11 October 2025}}</ref> It underpins international training programs and [[clinical trial]]s, including the 400-patient clinical trial EPINOV ("Improving epilepsy surgery management and prognosis using virtual brain technology") for [[Management of drug-resistant epilepsy|drug-resistant epilepsy]] where Jirsa serves as scientific director.<ref>{{cite web |title=Improving epilepsy care: HBP researchers involved in major clinical trial |url=https://www.humanbrainproject.eu/en/follow-hbp/news/improving-epilepsy-care-hbp-researchers-involved-in-major-clinical-trial/ |website=Human Brain Project |access-date=11 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Où en est le projet Epinov ? |url=https://region-sud.latribune.fr/innovation/2018-03-29/ou-en-est-le-projet-epinov-773675.html |website=La Tribune |date=29 March 2018 |access-date=11 October 2025}}</ref>

===Connectome-based brain models===

In the early 2000s, Jirsa was among the first to show that realistic [[white matter]] topology and conduction delays in the brain are essential for reproducing [[Resting state fMRI|fMRI resting state]] patterns, opening a field which is now central to [[network neuroscience]].<ref name="Jirsa pp. 1131–1143">{{cite journal | last=Jirsa | first=V | title=Neural field dynamics with local and ===Structured flows on manifolds (SFM)===
Structured flows on [[manifold]]s are mathematical objects that underlie the evolution of brain activity. Jirsa and colleagues showed that the brain's high-dimensional activity collapses onto low-dimensional spaces, where it follows emergent rule-based behavior ("flows"). SFM explain how [[connectome]]-driven breaking of symmetry yields a set of [[Trajectory|trajectories]] that reproduce resting state cascades and fast switching seen in [[Functional magnetic resonance imaging|fMRI]] and [[Magnetoencephalography|MEG]] scans.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=McIntosh R |author2=Jirsa V |title=The hidden repertoire of brain dynamics and dysfunction |journal=Network Neuroscience |date=September 2019 |volume=3 |issue=4 |pages=994–1008 |doi=10.1162/netn_a_00107 |s2cid=91716775 |pmid=31637335 |issn=2472-1751 |pmc=6777946}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Jirsa V |author2=McIntosh R |author3=Huys R |title=Grand Unified Theories of the Brain Need Better Understanding of Behavior: The Two-Tiered Emergence of Function |journal=Ecological Psychology |date=July 2019 |volume=31 |issue=3 |pages=152–165 |doi=10.1080/10407413.2019.1615207 |s2cid=199154486 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10407413.2019.1615207 |access-date=12 October 2025 |issn=1040-7413|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This SFM framework delivers guidelines for interventions that aim to bring the brain back onto healthy trajectories in [[Ageing|ageing]], [[Epilepsy|epilepsy]] and [[Mental disorder|psychiatric disorders]].

===Epileptor and seizure taxonomy===

[[Epilepsy]] is characterized by the onset and offset of high-frequency discharges visible in [[Electroencephalography|EEG]] scans of patients undergoing a [[seizure]]. Nonlinear [[Dynamical systems theory|dynamical system theory]] suggests that there is only a finite number of ways to start and stop an oscillation. Applying [[bifurcation theory]], Jirsa and colleagues derived a canonical model called "Epileptor" that reproduces 16 seizure "dynamotypes". The Epileptor explains stereotyped onsets and offsets across different species and predicts therapeutic windows, some of them validated clinically.<ref name="Naze Bernard Jirsa p=e1004209">{{cite journal | last1=Naze | first1=S | last2=Bernard | first2=C | last3=Jirsa | first3=V | editor-last=Graham | editor-first=L | title=Computational Modeling of Seizure Dynamics Using Coupled Neuronal Networks: Factors Shaping Epileptiform Activity | journal=PLOS Computational Biology | publisher=Public Library of Science (PLoS) | volume=11 | issue=5 | date=May 2015 | issn=1553-7358 | doi=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004209 | article-number=e1004209| pmid=25970348 | pmc=4430284 | bibcode=2015PLSCB..11E4209N | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Jirsa Stacey Quilichini Ivanov pp. 2210–2230">{{cite journal | last1=Jirsa | first1=V | last2=Stacey | first2=W | last3=Quilichini | first3=P | last4=Ivanov | first4=A | last5=Bernard | first5=C | title=On the nature of seizure dynamics | journal=Brain | publisher=Oxford University Press (OUP) | volume=137 | issue=8 | date=June 2014 | issn=1460-2156 | doi=10.1093/brain/awu133 | pages=2210–2230| pmid=24919973 | pmc=4107736 }}</ref><ref name="Proix Bartolomei Chauvel Bernard pp. 15009–15021">{{cite journal | last1=Proix | first1=T | last2=Bartolomei | first2=F | last3=Chauvel | first3=P | last4=Bernard | first4=C | last5=Jirsa | first5=V | title=Permittivity Coupling across Brain Regions Determines Seizure Recruitment in Partial Epilepsy | journal=Journal of Neuroscience | publisher=Society for Neuroscience | volume=34 | issue=45 | date=November 2014 | issn=0270-6474 | doi=10.1523/jneurosci.1570-14.2014 | pages=15009–15021| pmid=25378166 | pmc=6608363 }}</ref><ref name="El Houssaini Ivanov Bernard Jirsa p. ">{{cite journal | last1=El Houssaini | first1=K | last2=Ivanov | first2=A | last3=Bernard | first3=C | last4=Jirsa | first4=V | title=Seizures, refractory status epilepticus, and depolarization block as endogenous brain activities | journal=Physical Review E | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=91 | issue=1 | date=January 2015 | issn=1539-3755 | doi=10.1103/physreve.91.010701 | article-number=010701| pmid=25679555 | bibcode=2015PhRvE..91a0701E }}</ref>

The respective publication in ''[[Brain (journal)|Brain]]'' ([[Oxford University Press]]) was marked as "Editor's choice". In a commentary to Jirsa et al.'s publication,<ref name="Friston pp. 2110–2113">{{cite journal | last=Friston | first=K | title=On the modelling of seizure dynamics | journal=Brain | publisher=Oxford University Press (OUP) | volume=137 | issue=8 | date=July 2014 | issn=1460-2156 | doi=10.1093/brain/awu147 | pages=2110–2113| pmid=25057129 | pmc=4107741 }}</ref> neuroscientist and theoretician [[Karl Friston]] underlined the significant breakthrough of Jirsa's findings for the entire field of epilepsy.

===Digital twin medicine===
Since 2015 Jirsa is evolving his fundamental models into a personalized [[digital twin]] of the [[human brain]] with a focus on clinical application in precision [[neurology]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Jirsa V |author2=Proix T |author3=Perdikis D |author4=Woodman M |author5=Wang H |author6=Gonzalez-Martinez J |author7=Bernard C |author8=Bénar C |author9=Guye M |author10=Chauvel P |author11=Bartolomei F |title=The Virtual Epileptic Patient: Individualized whole-brain models of epilepsy spread |journal=NeuroImage |date=January 2017 |volume=145 |issue=Part B |pages=377–388 |doi=10.1016/j.neuroimage.2016.04.049 |s2cid=36510741 |pmid=27477535 |issn=1053-8119 |pmc=9543509}}</ref> He holds leading roles in European research projects (Virtual Brain Twin,<ref>{{cite web |title=Project / Team |url=https://www.virtualbraintwin.eu/project/team.html |website=Virtual Brain Twin |access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref> EBRAINS 2.0<ref>{{cite web |title=EBRAINS 2.0: 38 million to revolutionize digital neuroscience |url=https://www.univ-amu.fr/en/public/actualites/ebrains-20-38-million-revolutionize-digital-neuroscience |website=Aix-Marseille Université |date=2 June 2024 |access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref>) and French projects (Nautilus)<ref>{{cite web |title=Impact Santé: l'Inserm lance quatre projets de rupture pour la recherche en santé |url=https://presse.inserm.fr/impact-sante-linserm-lance-quatre-projets-de-rupture-pour-la-recherche-en-sante/69477/ |website=Institut National de la santé et de la recherche médicale (Inserm) |date=7 November 2024 |access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref> to extend the applicability of his models to [[Psychiatric medication|psychiatric drug]] response and [[Non-invasive procedure|non-invasive]] [[neurostimulation]].

==Awards and recognition==

Jirsa is invited regularly to major international conferences and has given more than 200 invited lectures, including various keynote addresses and plenary lectures, e.g. for [[Organization for Human Brain Mapping|OHBM]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Speakers - OHBM Educational Course on Whole-brain Models / OHBM 2023 |url=https://griffithslab.github.io/OHBM-whole-brain-modelling-course/speakers/ |website=OHBM 2023 / OHBM Educational Course on Whole-brain Models |publisher=Krembil Centre for Neuroinformatics - CAMH / Whole Brain Modelling Group |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref> [[International Neuroinformatics Coordinating Facility|INCF]]<ref>{{cite web |title=INCF Assembly 2024 |url=https://www.ebrains.eu/news-and-events/incf-assembly-2024 |website=EBRAINS |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref> or [[National Institutes of Health|NIH]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BRAIN Neuroethics Working Group (NEWG) Meeting – May 2025 / BRAIN Initiative |url=https://braininitiative.nih.gov/news-events/events/brain-neuroethics-working-group-newg-meeting-may-2025 |website=NIH Brain Initiative |publisher=National Institutes of Health / The BRAIN Initiative |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref>

He has been awarded several international and national awards for his research, including:

* 2025 Change the World – Rise Partners Innovation Award<ref>{{cite web |title=Les Trophées de l'Hypercroissance 2025 |url=https://www.risepartners.org/les-trophees-de-lhypercroissance-2025/ |website=Rise Partners |date=18 March 2025 |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref>
* 2021 First [[Human Brain Project]] Innovation Prize<ref>{{cite web |title=The first HBP innovation award went to the The[sic] Virtual Brain team and the next one is on its way! |url=https://www.humanbrainproject.eu/en/follow-hbp/news/the-first-hbp-innovation-award-went-to-the-the-virtual-brain-team-and-the-next-one-is-on-its-way/ |website=Human Brain Project |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref>
* 2018 Elected member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts|Academia Scientiarium et Artium Europaea]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Browse Members / European Academy of Sciences and Arts |url=https://members.euro-acad.eu |website=European Academy of Sciences and Arts |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref>
* 2018 Grand Prix de Recherche de Provence<ref>{{cite web |title=Prix départemental pour la recherche en Provence |url=https://www.departement13.fr/en-actions/enseignement-superieur-recherche/les-dispositifs/prix-departemental-pour-la-recherche-en |website=Département des Bouches-du-Rhône |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref>
* 2004 [[North American Society for the Psychology of Sport and Physical Activity|NASPSPA]] EarlyCareer Distinguished Scholar Award<ref>{{cite web |title=Awards |url=https://www.naspspa.com/awards/#past-recipients |website=NASPSPA (North American Society for the Psychology of Sport and Physical Activity) |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref>
* 2001 [[Information Processing in Medical Imaging#Past_Francois_Erbsmann_Prize_Winners|Francois Erbsmann Prize]] at the conference "[[Information Processing in Medical Imaging]]" (IPMI)
